fields.acceptance: internal/daemon roundrobin tests: with maxRuns 3, 2 running and one free slot, project A (turn next, 2 ready change sets) and project B (1 queued continuation), B's continuation takes the slot; with 2 free slots, A has a queued start and a ready change set and B has a continuation, the picks are B's continuation, then A's start; a project at its per-project max gets no continuation slot, and the slot goes to the next project's continuation, else its start; with no continuations queued, the existing roundrobin cases pick as before. daemon-round-robin.txtar and daemon-continue-slot.txtar still pass
fields.statement: The root daemon's round-robin (daemon.RoundRobin) fills freed machine-wide slots in three tiers: first every project's queued continuations that could start now, in round-robin order across projects; then queued starts and plan requests; then ready change sets. Each tier keeps each project's rhiza.project.maxRuns and the machine-wide maxRuns, and the rotation's last turn carries on as before. So a queued continuation never loses a freed slot to another project's start or roadmap pick. Counting is unchanged: an interrupted run takes no slot, and no run is pre-empted.

fields.acceptance: daemon-continue-slot.txtar with a fake rex: with max-runs 1 and one running run, two interrupted runs with rhiza run resume queued show in rhiza daemon status as interrupted, queued, waiting for a slot, at places 1 and 2, and --json gives each a queued place of 1 and 2; an interrupted run with nothing queued shows no queued place; describe-golden.txtar regenerated for the new response field
fields.statement: rhiza daemon status, in text and in --json (each live run's entry, per project under the root daemon), shows an interrupted run that has a queued continuation that could start as queued, waiting for a slot, with its place in its project's continuation queue (1 for the oldest), as well as interrupted. An interrupted run with nothing queued shows as before.
